summary: Democratic-Farmer-Labor Sen. Tina Smith did not seek re-election, so the seat was open. Peggy Flanagan (Democrat) defeated Michele Tafoya (Republican) and other candidates.

candidates.name: Peggy Flanagan
candidates.bio: Peggy Flanagan is the Democratic Lieutenant Governor of Minnesota and a former Minneapolis School Board member. She won the DFL endorsement and the August 2026 Democratic primary for the open Senate seat.

positions.summary: Says she will raise the federal minimum wage to $17 an hour, pass national paid family and medical leave, and expand the Child Tax Credit.
Says she will fight for Medicare for All, ban insurers' prior authorization, and restore the cuts to Minnesotans' health care.
Says she would dismantle ICE, end mass deportation policies, and create a path to legal status for long-term undocumented residents.
Says she would fully fund IDEA, expand Head Start and universal pre-K, and increase K-12 funding without vouchers.
Says she opposes rollbacks of clean energy investments and would expand wind and solar while supporting biofuels.
Says she would pass the Women's Health Protection Act to restore Roe v. Wade protections nationwide and repeal the Hyde Amendment.

candidates.name: Michele Tafoya
candidates.bio: Michele Tafoya is a Republican and former NFL sideline reporter, known for her work on NBC's Sunday Night Football. She launched her Senate campaign in January 2026.

positions.summary: Says she supports education reform that gives parents more say and increases transparency and accountability.
Says she opposes raising taxes on the middle class, wants to protect recent tax cuts for working families, and favors reducing federal spending and borrowing.
Says she wants to cut prescription drug prices and curb insurers and middlemen who raise costs.
Says she supports a secure border and deporting undocumented immigrants who have committed crimes, and opposes abolishing ICE.
Says she supports all U.S. energy sources to lower utility bills and gas prices while protecting the environment.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (political.org Nov 14 tally, AP called 34 of 35)
